in.other_title: No significant effect of debate turns or simultaneous vs sequential debate
in.rationale: Hammond and Adam-Day list not evaluating simultaneous versus sequential debate as a limitation of their own protocols, which they evaluate on only two domains, with a graph isomorphism task and a code-validation task. Sudhir et al. report no significant effect from switching between simultaneous and sequential debate or changing turn count, with a gpt-4o-mini judge on GSM8K, so the gap and the result concern different tasks; Hammond and Adam-Day train their agents, while the passage does not say whether Sudhir et al.'s debaters are trained.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether simultaneous versus sequential debate matters, for LLM debate on GSM8K

text: The authors list three limitations: their training algorithms do not use some of the more advanced methods described in Sections 4.1 and 4.2 (graph isomorphism task) or RL-based learning (code-validation task); they evaluate only two domains, far from representative of the tasks contemporary AI systems solve; and they do not evaluate all protocol variants, such as simultaneous versus sequential debate or open protocols where provers choose which outcome to argue for.
title: Limitations: simplified training, only two domains, untested protocol variants
